title: Sidney Bourgeois, the professor who was a tough fighter
summary: Williams describes Pop Torres's place, Sidney Bourgeois the mathematician and puncher, and his death by shooting.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Well, I'll tell you about Sidney Bourgeois, you read about the killing and all like that? Mm-hmm. Sidney Bourgeois used to come into Pop Toros, that's based on Bambler Street, where the piano players, well there's only a few of them, one played for Lilla White and one for Josie Arlington. Of course, Tony Jackson never come in there, see. Well, me and I used to hang out there. Pop Toros used to use us quite often, see. He got a dollar and I got two dollars a night, see. So I used to walk a meal home. He lived off Broad Street, and the next block back he had a home back there. And I walked back. I was standing at the Bush Hotel. So I passed, it was called the Budweiser, but it used to be like the Pup, the Pup was a beer hall. You know, I had a piano player and girls were sitting around there, just like the Hundred and One Ranch. And I barely passed there and Mamie Lee Kelly, I heard Mamie Lee Kelly, she was bumming Sidney Bourgeois. And he had a gun in his hands. A year before that, sometime before that, and I always say it's a year, he had picked up a policeman and threw him in a bread case across the street where there was a restaurant. Well, the police had it in for Sidney Bourgeois. So I passed there, I said, uh-uh. This party got across the street and heard the shots. Sidney Bourgeois was killed, see.
Did you tell him who? I'm telling the truth. Did you tell him who Sidney Bourgeois is? Who, if he knew who Sidney Bourgeois was?
No. No, I never did know him. Sidney Bourgeois was a professor.

He was a mathematician in the Spencer College. Oh. We had a pop tour, he'd come in, put your figures down, nines and eights and sevens and mix them all up. Very smart man. Boom, boom, boom, boom. Right to answer. But when he was in, he was in pop tours one day, he was a well, a good dresser, Sidney Bourgeois. And the gentleman with him had nice clothes on. All at once, boom, he hit his friend. For what?

Sidney Bourgeois hit his friend? Oh, he was a terrific puncher. When he was a professor, when he got to drinking, he was a tough man. He was really tough. And if he hit you one time, he was going. He was a tough puncher. Take two, three men to take care of him, the guy he's tough.
So, Stadbury and I sat on that, far from it, and Stadbury walks over to Sidney, and said, don't you ever hit me. Stadbury can fight. I got a group of friends.
You know something? Maybe you might not be mentioning names because they might sue you. You might have some relatives living here.
I don't think they can do that. Huh? They can.
I mean, he's been dead a while. Well, that's an old faculty telling me. Yeah.
